description: Case ID, activity and timestamp are populated on every event
implication: A null in any of these makes the event unusable for process mining; the row would have to be dropped.

Timestamps are minute-precision, so several updates within the same minute collapse onto one value. The fact table therefore needs a surrogate event key and an explicit within-case sequence number, not a natural key.
Exact duplicates would double-count volume and distort dwell times.
Confirms the source uses day-first European format. Parsing these as month-first would silently corrupt every duration in the project.

description: Columns at least 90% unknown are identified
implication: These carry almost no signal. They are excluded from the dimensional model rather than shipped as near-empty attributes that invite false conclusions.

description: Every incident_state is a recognised process activity
implication: Sentinel values like '-100' are source-system artefacts, not real process steps. Left in, they appear as a phantom activity in the process map.

description: Cases ending in Resolved/Closed carry a resolved_at timestamp
observed: 1,556 of 21,668 terminal cases have resolved_at unknown
implication: Cycle time cannot be computed for these; they must be excluded from the cycle-time denominator rather than counted as zero duration.

description: closed_at is distributed, not concentrated on batch timestamps
implication: A handful of timestamps account for a large share of all closures: an automated bulk-close job, not real agent activity. closed_at is therefore NOT a valid basis for cycle time. resolved_at is used instead.

description: made_sla is constant across all events of a case
implication: made_sla is a live evaluation that flips the moment the clock is breached, not a static outcome. Counting it at event grain would overstate attainment. The case-grain fact must take the LAST observed value per case.

description: Events within a case are chronologically consistent
implication: Negative dwell times would corrupt bottleneck analysis.

description: resolved_at is never earlier than opened_at
observed: 0 events of 138,571 comparable have resolved_at < opened_at
implication: Negative cycle times must be quarantined, never averaged in.

description: Case-level attributes are stable across a case's events
observed: cases with more than one distinct value: {'priority': 383, 'category': 1216, 'contact_type': 5, 'caller_id': 3}
implication: Attributes that change mid-case cannot be modelled as static case dimensions; the case-grain fact takes the last observed value, consistent with DQ-09.
